title: Townhouse weathertightness remedial recladding: CCC refusal; District Court appeal attached (Paremata, Porirua)
jurisdiction: New Zealand (MBIE, Building Act 2004): comparative test only; not an Alberta case; no Alberta applicability asserted
code_edition: Clauses current when the consent was issued (App. A3, p.39–40)
document_type: MBIE determination under Building Act 2004 s188 (regulator decision on an individual matter); not an applicant's alternative-solution file

facts.text: Remediation of a townhouse in a 12-unit development at Paremata, Porirua; authority refused a CCC citing B1, B2 and E2.
Determination considers the cladding and its fixings; the timber framing is outside the determination.
Determination finds that remediation of damaged structural elements was not a requirement of the consent, so the refusal on that ground was incorrect.
Expert findings: the cladding is compliant with B2 insofar as it applies to B1; no evidence of contemporary weathertightness issues from the remediation.
Decision: authority's refusal of the CCC for the reasons in its letter of 9 March 2015 is incorrect; reversed and a new decision required (30 September 2022).
Companion attachment: Porirua City Council v Gault [2024] NZDC 19464 (CIV-2022-085-000665, Judge L I Hinton): council's s208(1)(b) appeal dismissed and the determination confirmed (para [100]).

limitations: Comparative only: a New Zealand determination used to test attachment format and content; it cannot establish Alberta performance or applicability.
